answer: A sybil swarm is cheap only while identities cost nothing, so the counterweight is a bonded registry: each agent stakes collateral that peers slash if its claims prove false. Every copy must carry its own bond, so ten thousand lookalikes is not a hollow boast but ten thousand deposits genuinely at risk. An honest agent holding a pearl of reputation gains nothing by splitting into clones, since staked value burns once peers cross-check a false claim. The ledger is a jetty where only staked vessels dock. Impostor cost scales with headcount, which makes mass fraud unprofitable.
